title: FinerDedup: Sifting Fingerprints for Efficient Data Deduplication on Mobile Devices
problem: Existing data deduplication systems consume excessive memory and incur high indexing costs for maintaining fingerprints for each data block on mobile devices, where duplicate ratios are only 10-30%.
motivation: Improving storage capacity and lifetime of mobile devices through more efficient data deduplication.
method: FinerDedup uses a random forest classifier combined with Bloom filters to identify and screen out duplicate data blocks before creating fingerprints, reducing the total number of fingerprints required. The system pre-filters data blocks to classify potential duplicates without full fingerprint computation, maintaining retrieval efficiency while reducing memory overhead.
key_novelty: Using random forest and Bloom filter together to pre-filter and eliminate unnecessary fingerprints for duplicate data blocks.
contributions: Reduces fingerprint count by 85% compared to DmDedup
Reduces I/O latency by 20% over DmDedup
Optimizes memory consumption and indexing costs for mobile deduplication systems
Implementation and evaluation on real Android 10 devices with real mobile workloads
primary_theme: Efficient data deduplication for mobile storage
